blocks.text: The Minimum Charge Problem for Small Suites

Ground-floor window washing has a simple cost structure: travel, setup, and the labor to clean the glass. For a large building, the labor dominates. For a small suite, travel and setup dominate, and vendors recover them with a trip minimum, typically $90 to $135 per visit. A 2,000 sq ft office in a strip center might have a glass door, two sidelights, and two storefront windows totaling around 150 sq ft of glass. A technician can clean that exterior in 10 to 15 minutes, yet the invoice reflects a full minimum. That is why small offices often see effective rates of $0.60 to $0.90 per sq ft of glass while their neighbors in larger buildings pay a fraction of that.

Large buildings flip the equation. A 30,000 sq ft corporate office with a glass lobby and ground-floor windows along three elevations can have 3,000 to 5,000 sq ft of reachable glass. A crew working continuous runs with water-fed poles covers 1,000 to 1,500 sq ft per technician hour, and the one-time setup is trivial relative to the work. Unit costs fall toward $0.15 to $0.22 per sq ft.

blocks.text: The steepest drop happens between 2,000 and 10,000 sq ft of office space, as glass inventory grows enough to escape the minimum. Beyond about 25,000 sq ft the curve flattens, because labor is already the main component and there is little remaining overhead to spread. At that point, savings come from frequency planning and scope design rather than additional volume.

blocks.title: Labor floor
blocks.text: At specialty labor rates of $55–$95 per hour and production of 1,000–1,500 sq ft of exterior glass per hour, pure labor cost is roughly $0.04–$0.10 per sq ft. Large-building quotes near $0.15–$0.22 include travel, pure-water equipment, insurance, and margin. Quotes below $0.12 on large glass areas warrant questions about thoroughness.

Small offices cannot add glass, but they can share or absorb the minimum. The most effective tactic is a multi-tenant route: coordinate with neighboring suites in the same strip center or office park so one vendor visits all of them on the same day. Each tenant pays a reduced per-suite rate, often $45 to $75, because the vendor's trip charge is shared. Property managers can facilitate this through a center-wide window contract and pass the cost through common area maintenance charges.

items: Join or organize a shared route with neighboring tenants to split the trip minimum.
Bundle exterior windows with your janitorial vendor's regular visit so no separate trip is billed.
Choose exterior-only monthly service and have your janitorial crew spot-clean interior glass.
Schedule both-sides cleaning quarterly instead of monthly to reduce the number of minimum charges.
Ask your landlord whether storefront glass is already covered under CAM services.

blocks.text: Bundling with janitorial service is the other strong option. If your nightly or weekly cleaning crew is already on site, adding a monthly exterior pass of 150 sq ft of reachable glass might add only $25 to $40 per month because no separate trip occurs. Confirm that the janitorial vendor's certificate of insurance covers exterior work and that crew members have proper pole equipment for a streak-free finish.

Large buildings should focus on zoning and frequency. Not every elevation needs the same schedule. Main entrances and lobby glass facing the parking lot are seen by every visitor and may warrant twice-monthly service, while side and rear elevations facing service drives can go quarterly. Splitting a 4,000 sq ft glass inventory into a 1,200 sq ft high-visibility zone cleaned twice monthly and a 2,800 sq ft secondary zone cleaned quarterly can cut annual spend by 35% to 50% compared with cleaning everything monthly.

Large sites also benefit from coordinating exterior glass with lobby floor care, since entry glass and entry floors share the same soil sources. A lobby running a cordless compact scrubber such as the Karcher BD 30/4 C Bp, with an 11-inch scrub path and 1-gallon tanks, can be scrubbed the same morning the windows are washed to catch runoff and tracked grit at the doors. Facilities with VCT entries may use a 20-inch, 175 RPM rotary machine like the Sanitaire SC6045A for periodic scrubbing of entry vestibules. In restrooms near lobbies, simple odor control such as Fresh Products Wave 3D urinal screens, with a 30-day enzymatic life, is often bundled into the same day-porter route that manages lobby appearance, though it is unrelated to window pricing itself.

blocks.text: Writing a Scope That Fits Your Size

items.name: Measure reachable glass
items.text: Measure glass reachable from the ground on each elevation, noting which sides need cleaning and any landscaping or obstructions.

items.name: Pick a pricing basis
items.text: Small suites should ask for flat per-visit pricing; large buildings should request per-sq-ft rates by zone.

items.name: Define zones and frequency
items.text: Assign high-visibility and secondary zones with separate schedules to match appearance priorities.

items.name: List inclusions and exclusions
items.text: Include frames and sills; exclude screens, hard-water restoration, and glass above ground-floor reach unless priced separately.

items.name: Confirm compliance documents
items.text: Collect a COI naming your company and landlord, workers' compensation proof, and SDS sheets for any cleaning chemicals.

blocks.title: Frequency math check
blocks.text: When comparing a monthly flat fee against per-visit pricing, remember twice-monthly service averages about 2.17 visits per month based on 4.333 weeks per month, so a $200 per-visit rate equals roughly $434 per month, not $400.

faqs.q: Why does my small office pay so much per square foot for window washing?
faqs.a: Small offices usually trigger the vendor's trip minimum of $90–$135, even if the glass takes only 10 to 15 minutes to clean. That pushes the effective cost to $0.60–$0.90 per sq ft of glass. Sharing a route with neighboring tenants or bundling windows with your janitorial visit are the most effective ways to lower the effective rate.

faqs.q: At what building size does window washing get cheaper per square foot?
faqs.a: The biggest drop happens as ground-floor glass grows past about 500 to 900 sq ft, typically in buildings around 5,000 to 10,000 sq ft. Beyond roughly 25,000 sq ft, unit costs level off at $0.15–$0.22 per sq ft of glass, and further savings come from zoning and frequency rather than volume.

faqs.q: Can my janitorial vendor wash exterior ground-floor windows?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the glass is reachable from the ground with poles. Confirm the vendor's certificate of insurance covers exterior work, that workers' compensation is in force, and that crews follow OSHA ladder safety rules if any ladder use is required. Glass above the ground floor normally calls for a specialized window contractor.

faqs.q: How should a large building schedule ground-floor window washing?
faqs.a: Zone the building by visibility. Main entrances and lobby glass often justify twice-monthly service, while side and rear elevations can be cleaned quarterly. This approach typically reduces annual spend by 35%–50% compared with cleaning all glass monthly, without visible decline at key entries.

faqs.q: What should be excluded from a standard ground-floor window quote?
faqs.a: Screen cleaning, deep track cleaning, hard-water stain restoration, construction residue removal, and glass beyond ground-floor reach are commonly excluded and priced separately. Hard-water restoration uses acidic products, so request SDS sheets and confirm crews use appropriate PPE under OSHA Hazard Communication rules.
